articles.title: WXV Global Series: England's draw with Canada can help Red Roses to greater things - John Mitchell
articles.summary: Head coach John Mitchell says England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak.
articles.body:
Head coach John Mitchell believes England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak.

England had won their past 39 Tests before Saturday's fixture.

Canada, who had lost their 13 previous meetings with the Red Roses on English soil, held England to a 26-26 draw in a nail-biting, physical battle at Exeter's Sandy Park.

It was only the second game domestically or internationally for England's players this season and, for Mitchell, one result is not justification to tear up the playbook.

Instead, he views it as a building block towards future success.

"It was just a matter of scoring across the white line," Mitchell said. "We were applying huge pressure. We just didn't convert."

Avoiding defeat means the Red Roses have extended their unbeaten run to 40 matches, a record they will hope to extend with WXV Global Series games against New Zealand, two more fixtures against Canada and another against the United States still to come.

Mitchell said: "There was such good stuff in there. I'm very patient because we're just starting and we're still alive in this Test series.

"I'm a realist. There will be greater things come as a result of this. There's a greater purpose and one Test match is not going to take us away from our purpose."

For the opening 10 minutes, the match followed the script of last year's World Cup final between the two sides, with Canada breaking the deadlock and England immediately hitting back.

But unlike last September, when they roared on to win 33-13, the Red Roses could not maintain control, with the two teams never separated by more than one try and England unable to convert 20 minutes of sustained pressure into the crucial score.

While acknowledging England would have to review their "game management", captain Meg Jones hailed the spectacle the two sides delivered.

"It was definitely tit for tat and definitely a game of momentum swinging," said centre Jones. "It was two good teams going at each other.

"It was an amazing contest and competitive as we imagined. This is the first Test. We get another two shots at it [against Canada]."

Echoing Jones' defiance before October trips to Toronto and Ottawa, Mitchell added: "We're in a Test series. It's 1-1. That's it."

Winning run has 'just been there' - Jones

England's 39-game winning run started under former head coach Simon Middleton, who, after the World Cup final defeat in 2022, led the Red Roses to a Women's Six Nations Grand Slam in 2023.

Mitchell then took charge midway through the 2023 WXV1 campaign and had won every game until this one.

England beat Scotland in the World Cup quarter-finals last September to claim their 31st straight Test win, surpassing their own record winning streak across both men's and women's international rugby union, which was set in 2022.

World Cup glory, another Women's Six Nations title and victory over Australia last weekend extended that record further.

"It's not necessarily something we speak about as a group; it's something that's just been there," Jones said of the winning run.

"We're very process-driven, so the outcome tends to look after itself."

articles.title: Welsh rugby's key signings ahead of 2026-27 season
articles.summary: Four summer signings are tipped to make a big impact at Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets in the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship.
articles.body:
Wales' regions may have seen more star names depart but the summer has also seen one of the most active recruitment drives in recent years.

There were notable departures with the loss of Jac Morgan, Dewi Lake, Aaron Wainwright and Marnus van der Merwe.

And Welsh professional men's rugby continues to be hit by off-field uncertainty with the WRU committed to cutting the number of regions from four to three.

But Cardiff, Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets - now all signed up to the new participation agreement and an increase in annual budget - have made significant additions as they seek old heads and overseas talent to help develop young homegrown squads for the 2026-27 season.

BBC Sport Wales looks at which signings could have a big say on whether the season is a success.

Only a handful of players have made the short but telling switch between west Wales rivals Scarlets and Ospreys.

Jac Morgan and Gavin Henson began their careers in Llanelli before making a name in Swansea while Lee Byrne was already a Test player when he moved in the same direction.

But Tom Rogers already had a place in history when - as a Scarlet - he became the first Wales player to score three tries against New Zealand last November.

He had number 11 on his back on that occasion but has moved to St Helen's with the aim of pushing for more caps wearing 15.

Rogers, who believes he is a better full-back than wing, could provide Ospreys with a different sort of threat from deep after the departure of Jack Walsh.

Head coach Mark Jones said: "Tom is a bit of a Swiss Army Knife in the fact he is equally adept at full-back and wing, and we have no doubt that he will hit the ground running."

Ospreys also have Lewis Edwards coming through after he impressed with his big boot for Wales at the World Rugby U20 Championship - but 27-year-old Rogers will aim to make the 15 jersey his own in Swansea.

Gareth Anscombe will certainly be an influence off the pitch at Scarlets with the experience of 37 Test caps, two World Cup campaigns and a Grand Slam.

How much the 35-year-old will impact matters on the pitch will likely depend on his ability to remain fit.

Amscombe's career has been beset by injury and arrives at Parc y Scarlets on the back of just five appeances last season for Bayonne.

In fact he has only twice manged double figures a season for a club - Ospreys in 2021-22 and Gloucester in 2024-25 - since rupturing knee ligaments in 2019.

Scarlets have signed him to provide competition for Wales playmaker Sam Costelow and ensure Joe Hawkins remains in his favoured position of inside centre.

Anscombe also arrives to help develop teenager Carwyn Leggatt-Jones, who was thrust into the starting line-up last season due to injuries and unavailability.

"I feel like I've got a nice place to fill in supporting those young guys," he told the Scrum V podcast .

"I would love to see Sam and Carwyn progress and have long careers ahead of them.

"I want to be playing a bit, supporting the group and hopefully passing on some knowledge I've learned over my career."

Cardiff have plenty of firepower in the backs but need to provide a platform if they are to make the next step.

The Blue and Blacks qualified for the play-offs last season by finishing sixth but were comprehensively beaten by Stormers in the quarter-finals.

"It is obvious, our set-piece needs to improve," said flanker Dan Thomas in the immediate aftermath of the Cape Town loss.

"The Stormers were dominant and we didn't cope. We knew it was coming and still couldn't stop it."

Loose-head prop Scott Sio, who won 74 caps for Australia, arrives from Exeter charged with helping to drive improvement in that department.

"One of the biggest things Cardiff want to pride themselves on is that set-piece," said the 34-year-old.

"Hopefully I can be a good cog in the wheel there and provide some experience."

Sio made the last of his 86 appearances for Chiefs in June's Prem final at Twickenham and still harbours ambitions of reaching a third World Cup , now with Samoa.

"He is very experienced and wants to look after the boys around him in the changing room, in the gym, on the pitch," said head coach Corniel van Zyl.

Dragons had their quietest summer for many years, focusing on retention rather than recruitment.

Filo Tiatia has added just three senior players to his squad - Tonga wing Anzelo Tuitavuki, Samoa scrum-half Ereatara Enari and back-row forward Terrell Peita from New Zealand.

Enari arrives fresh from winning Super Rugby with Hurricanes - he was All Blacks scrum-half Cam Roigard's deputy but was trusted with regular minutes when making 15 appearances in the successful campaign.

"He's a winner, a tough and competitive nine with a big engine and good in defence. He's also got that X-Factor abut him, and you see that with him scoring tries," said Dragons defence coach Dale MacLeod.

The 29-year-old will battle with Wales hopeful Che Hope, Morgan Lloyd and Wales veteran Rhodri Williams but has also been signed for his leadership.
